items.stem: Distinguish between 'social movement' and 'counter-movement'.
items.answer: Social movement: sustained collective action over time, often directed against the state, with shared objectives, ideology and some form of organisation. Counter-movement: a movement that arises to defend the status quo against a social movement, such as the Dharma Sabha against the campaign to abolish sati.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: 1 mark for explaining 'social movement' (sustained collective action over time, often directed against the state, with shared objectives, ideology and some form of organisation.) and 1 mark for 'counter-movement' (a movement that arises to defend the status quo against a social movement, such as the Dharma Sabha against the campaign to abolish sati.), with the contrast between them made clear.

items.answer: Mancur Olson's theory that individuals act in social movements out of rational self-interest, joining only if they gain from it

items.stem: Distinguish between 'Chipko movement' and 'Tebhaga movement'.
items.answer: Chipko movement: the ecological movement in the Himalayan region in which villagers, especially women, hugged trees to prevent them from being cut by contractors. Tebhaga movement: the 1946–47 struggle of sharecroppers in Bengal for two-thirds of the harvest.
items.markingKey: 2 marks: 1 mark for explaining 'Chipko movement' (the ecological movement in the Himalayan region in which villagers, especially women, hugged trees to prevent them from being cut by contractors.) and 1 mark for 'Tebhaga movement' (the 1946–47 struggle of sharecroppers in Bengal for two-thirds of the harvest.), with the contrast between them made clear.
